set system host-name [parameter1].explanation: Configure the host name of the device.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.explanation: The host name of the equipment is used to identify the equipment in the network.

set protocols mpls interface [parameter1.explanation: Enables the MPLS protocol on the specified interface.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: Interface name, e.g., g-1/0/0.

set protocols ldp transport-address [par.explanation: Configures the transfer address for the LDP protocol.

parameters.name: transport-address
parameters.explanation: the transfer address of the LDP protocol.

set protocols ldp targeted-peer [paramet.explanation: Configure the target peer for the LDP protocol.

parameters.name: targeted-peer
parameters.explanation: The target peer address for the LDP protocol, for example, 1.1.1.9.

set protocols ldp discovery interface [p.command: set protocols ldp discovery interface lo0.1
set protocols ldp discovery interface [p.explanation: Configures the LDP protocol to find the neighbor on the specified interface.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: The name of the interface, on which the LDP protocol will be found by the neighbour.

set routing-instances [parameter1].explanation: This command fragment configures a routing instance named `[parameter1]` in Junos, allowing for separate routing tables and protocols within that instance.

parameters.name: routing-instance
parameters.explanation: Name of route example, e.g. net.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: Interface name, e.g., g-1/0/2.

route-distinguisher [parameter2].explanation: The command `route-distinguisher [parameter2]` assigns a unique Route Distinguisher (RD) to a VPN routing instance, enabling distinct routing tables for overlapping IP addresses.

parameters.name: ip-address
parameters.explanation: The IP address portion of the route distinguisher, for example, 4.4.4.9.

:[parameter3].explanation: The command fragment `:[parameter3]` in Junos is used to reference or pass a specific parameter (parameter3) within a script or configuration context.

parameters.name: number
parameters.explanation: The numeric part of the route distinguisher, for example, 100.

vrf-target [parameter2].explanation: The command `vrf-target [parameter2]` in Junos configures a route target for a VRF, enabling the import/export of routes in a VPN.

parameters.name: target-type
parameters.explanation: The type of VRF target, for example, "target."

:[parameter3].explanation: The command fragment `:[parameter3]` in Junos is used to reference or pass a specific parameter (parameter3) within a script or operational mode command.

parameters.name: as-number
parameters.explanation: The AS number part of the VRF target, for example, 100.

:[parameter4].explanation: The command fragment `:[parameter4]` in Junos is a placeholder for a specific parameter value, typically used in operational mode to filter or specify details in command output.

parameters.name: number
parameters.explanation: The numeric part of the VRF target, for example, 100.

set protocols l2circuit neighbor [parame.explanation: Configures a Layer 2 Circuit (L2Circuit) neighbor with the specified IP address (`[parameter1]`) for point-to-point pseudowire connectivity.

parameters.name: neighbor-ip
parameters.explanation: Neighbor's IP address.

interface [parameter2].explanation: This command configures a Layer 2 Circuit (L2Circuit) by specifying a neighbor device (`parameter1`) and associating it with a local interface (`parameter2`) for pseudowire establishment.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: interface name.

virtual-circuit-id [parameter3].explanation: The L2 circuit is equipped with neighbours, interfaces and virtual circuit ID.

parameters.name: virtual-circuit-id
parameters.explanation: Virtual circuit identifier.

encapsulation-type [parameter4].explanation: Configure L2VPN neighbours, interfaces, virtual circuit ID and containment types.

parameters.name: encapsulation-type
parameters.explanation: Cover type, e.g. vlan.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: Interface name, e.g., g-1/0/0.

vlan-tagging.explanation: Configure the VLAN tag for the interface.

unit [parameter2].explanation: Configure the unit number of the interface.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit numbers that distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

vlan-id [parameter3].explanation: Configure VLAN IDs for interface units.

parameters.name: vlan-id
parameters.explanation: VLAN ID, used to identify VLAN.

encapsulation [parameter3].explanation: Configure the envelope type of the interface.

parameters.name: encapsulation
parameters.explanation: Cover type, e.g., pp.

family inet address [parameter3]/[parame.explanation: Configure IPv4 addresses for interfaces and subnet masks.

parameters.name: ip-address
parameters.explanation: The IPv4 address assigned to the interface.

parameters.name: subnet-mask
parameters.explanation: Bits of IPv4 subnet mask.

family [parameter3].explanation: Enables the MPLS protocol on the interface.

parameters.name: family
parameters.explanation: Protocol, for example.

set protocols rsvp interface [parameter1.explanation: Configure the interface for the RSVP protocol.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: Interface name, for example, ge-5/0/0.

set protocols ospf area [parameter1].explanation: This command configures an OSPF area in Junos OS, where `[parameter1]` specifies the area ID, enabling OSPF routing within the defined area.

parameters.name: area
parameters.explanation: OSPF area ID.

interface [parameter2].explanation: Configure interfaces in the OSPF area.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: Interface name, e.g., g-1/0/0.0.

set protocols ospf traffic-engineering.explanation: Enables the flow engineering function of the OSF protocol.
